To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) stroke survivors are willing and motivated to use tangible stroke rehabilitation systems in their home, 2) tangible stroke rehabilitation systems should support self-awareness and be tailored to the individual, and 3) tangible stroke rehabilitation should focus on activities of daily living.

tangible stroke rehabilitation systems should be designed to be easily tailorable in order to support the individual rehabilitation requirements of stroke survivors, and should support self-awareness and the practice of grip exercises in order for stroke survivors to become more independent in activities of daily living.

stroke rehabilitation in the home can be improved by using bimanual tangible interfaces that allow the user to customize the device to their needs and that provide feedback to the user to improve awareness of their abilities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
designing tangible stroke rehabilitation systems to support stroke rehabilitation in the home.
the design of tangible rehabilitation systems that support bimanual exercises in the home, and that are tailored towards stroke survivors’ individual needs.
the development of interactive tangible bimanal devices for stroke rehabilitation in the home.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

tangible stroke rehabilitation systems should be designed to support the stroke survivor in their own home, and that the tangible stroke rehabilitation systems need to be tailored to the individual stroke survivor.

tangible devices can help stroke survivors to increase their independency in activities of daily living and that they should be tailored to the individual needs and preferences of the stroke survivor in order to increase motivation.

tangible bimanual systems can support upper limb stroke rehabilitation in the home and that the design of such a system should consider tailorable form factor, self-awareness exercises, grip exercises, and the ability to adapt to the user’s individual needs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
stroke rehabilitation in the home is possible with the use of tangible devices, and that these devices need to be tailored to the needs and preferences of stroke survivors.
stroke rehabilitation systems should be designed with a focus on supporting the stroke survivor in the long run and in their daily lives.
tangible stroke rehabilitation devices can support stroke survivors to increase their independency in the home.
The main takeaway from our work is that

interactive tangible bimanal devices can be used to support upper limb stroke rehabilitation in the home, and that these devices need to support self-awareness and self-motivation in order to increase independence of stroke survivors.
tangible bimanual rehabilitation systems for stroke rehabilitation should focus on supporting stroke survivors to carryout daily activities and to be aware of their own motor function impairments.
